reading.body:
Oregon has four bills addressing AI directly: one on AI companions, one on AI generally, one on journalism compensation in an AI context, and one on downcoding, all filed in early 2026.

The state is not creating a single AI regulatory framework but responding to discrete problems. SB1546 targets a specific application. HB4103 addresses AI broadly without a stated focus. SB1580 treats AI as a threat to a particular industry's business model rather than a technology risk. This patchwork approach mirrors how most states regulate emerging technology, responding to constituency pressure rather than systemic questions.

None of these bills describe themselves as relating to compute, power, or infrastructure. The data does not indicate whether Oregon is considering or constraining the physical prerequisites that AI scaling requires. Without seeing bill text, it is impossible to know whether any bill would affect data center development, electricity grid planning, or semiconductor supply chains in the state.
